name: Hatanodai
tagline: Shinagawa in 18 minutes and Shibuya in 23 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000.
summary: The station is in Shinagawa City, where Tokyu run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 36 minutes to Otemachi, 31 minutes to Shinjuku, 23 minutes to Shibuya and 18 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. The station stands 23.5 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 15.8 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 23.5 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 19.4 m to 35.2 m, a difference of 15.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 2 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 22 clinics and 16 pharmacies. The nearest hospital is 昭和医科大学病院, about 6 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is おきの会旗の台病院, about 6 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: Tokyu Oimachi Line and Tokyu Ikegami Line. Both lines are run by Tokyu, so a fault affecting that company can stop them together.
congestion: Tokyu Ikegami Line runs at 130% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 大崎広小路→五反田, which this station is not on. Tokyu Oimachi Line runs at 118%. Its busiest stretch is 九品仏→自由が丘, which this station is likewise not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: One room ¥80,000 to ¥90,000, 1K ¥90,000 to ¥100,000, 1LDK ¥160,000 to ¥170,000 and 2LDK ¥230,000 to ¥240,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 9 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Among the 23 wards' stations, very few of the points around this one fall inside the projected inundation area for the largest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. The choice of connections is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are lightly loaded in the morning.
